title: Humility after learning
hookLine: and above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing (12:76)

lines: YUSUF, THE CUP, THE BROTHER'S BAG.
cards: "And over every lord of knowledge there is one more knowing." That's half a verse of the Qur'an, in Pickthall's translation, and it turns up in the middle of a family drama.
Yusuf, now powerful in Egypt, has had a royal cup hidden in his brother's bag, so that he can keep him close. The plan works.
And right there, the verse says the plan was Allah's doing for Yusuf, then steps back and adds: there is always someone who knows more.

teach.h: RAISED BY DEGREES, NEVER AT THE TOP.
MUSA SAYS I, THEN WALKS TO LEARN.
teach.b: Its full line says that Allah raises by degrees whom He will, and then: over every lord of knowledge there is one more knowing. Knowledge is real, and it lifts people.
It also never reaches a top shelf a human can stand on. Second, a prophet learns it. Five days ago, Musa set out for the meeting of the two seas.
A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari tells how that journey began. Musa is asked who is the most learned of people, and he answers: I am.
Allah reproaches him, in the hadith's telling, because he did not refer the knowledge back to Allah, and tells him of a servant who knows more.

In the Qur'an Musa asks that servant, in paraphrase: may I follow you, so that you teach me some of the right guidance you were taught? A prophet becomes a student again. Third, even the angels say it.

teach.h: THE ANGELS: ONLY WHAT YOU TAUGHT US.
teach.b: When Adam is taught the names, the angels answer, in paraphrase: glory be to You, we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Fourth, the words people use.

teach.h: ALLAH KNOWS BEST. I DON'T KNOW.
teach.b: Muslim teachers may close an answer with Allahu a'lam, Allah knows best. And a story people tell about Imam Malik has him answering question after question in one sitting with: I don't know.

Whether or not every detail holds, the habit it praises is the one in the verse. Four years of lessons, in the verse's own terms, are a step, not the summit. Someone knows more, and above them, someone more again.

how: Muslim scholars and teachers end a ruling or an answer with Allahu a'lam, Allah knows best, and students are taught to say I don't know rather than guess about the religion.

o: refusing to study, since only Allah truly knows things
knowing that however much you learn, someone knows more
pretending not to know, so no one thinks you're proud

games.q: humility after learning — tap the pairs.
p: said I, then walked to learn
only what You have taught us

s: in the hadith, Musa answers that someone else is the most learned
he says I am, and Allah reproaches him for not referring knowledge back to Allah.
the verse about one more knowing comes in the story of Yusuf
it follows the cup hidden in his brother's bag, in surah 12.
the angels claim knowledge of their own
they say they know only what Allah has taught them.

games.q: you are Musa. someone asks: who is the most learned of people? what do you answer?
games.why: in Sahih al-Bukhari Musa says I am, and Allah reproaches him for not referring the knowledge back to Allah, then sends him to learn from someone who knows more.

practice: Look for one thing from this year you've talked about as if you were sure, a ruling, a story, a meaning, and you're not. Name it plainly to yourself, I don't actually know this, and let the not-knowing be true for a minute.
If you pray, you can add the words Muslims use: Allahu a'lam, Allah knows best.

wordCard.voice: Humility after learning. The more you learn, the clearer it gets that over every lord of knowledge is one more knowing. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: one who knows; the last word of the line in 12:76, and al-'Alim, the All-Knowing, is a name of Allah.

carryVoice: Your line: someone knows more. Even a prophet walked a long way to learn. Rest well.
